title: Forms IV, V, VI, VII, VIII and X

blocks.text: In A2-17 you have studied forms II and III. Other derived forms are recognized by prefixes and schemes: ⁧أَرْسَلَ⁩ (IV), ⁧تَكَلَّمَ⁩ ( V), ⁧تَعَاوَنَ⁩ (VI) ⁧اِنْقَطَعَ⁩ (VII), ⁧اِجْتَمَعَ⁩ (III), ⁧اِسْتَقْبَلَ⁩ ( X). Many of these verbs have been using them for months ( ⁧أَعْطَى⁩ , ⁧تَعَلَّمَ⁩ , ⁧اِنْتَظَرَ⁩ , ⁧اِتَّصَلَ⁩ , ⁧اِسْتَطَاعَ⁩ ); Here you put them in a unique system. The objective of A2 is to recognize: given a word in a title without vowels, find the root, form and sense, and know how to read the maṣdar and the participle. News is the ideal ground: it's full of derived forms. A week.

blocks.text: 1. Remove the imperfect person prefix ( ⁧يَـ⁩ , ⁧تَـ⁩ , ⁧أَ⁩ , ⁧نَـ⁩ / ⁧يُـ⁩ ...) and terminations ( ⁧ـونَ⁩ , ⁧ـتُ⁩ , ⁧ـوا⁩ …).
2. Look at the beginning: ⁧أَ⁩ to the perfect → IV; ⁧تَـ⁩ + double → V; ⁧تَـ⁩ + ⁧ا⁩ → VI; ⁧اِنْـ⁩ → VII (or VIII with root in ⁧ن⁩ ); ⁧اِ⁩ _ ⁧تَ⁩ → VIII;
⁧اِسْتَـ⁩ → X; ⁧مُ⁩ ... → participle; ⁧تَفْعِيل⁩ , ⁧إِفْعَال⁩ , ⁧اِفْتِعَال⁩ , ⁧اِسْتِفْعَال⁩ → maṣdar.
3. Look at the center: double → II or V; ā after the first radical → III or VI.
4. There are three letters left: it is the root. Search in the dictionary and choose the right way to form.

Without vowels, forms II and I are confused ( ⁧درس⁩ , ⁧علم⁩ ), as well as IV and I in some people ( ⁧أرسل⁩ is IV, but ⁧أكتب⁩ "Write is I": use context and, to the imperfect, difference ⁧يُرْسِلُ⁩ / ⁧يَكْتُبُ⁩ , but you can't see without vowels. The forms III, V, VI, VII, VIII, X instead are almost always recognized even without vowels.

blocks.text: Choose one of the texts read in this form (A2-13 → A2-17) or a short article found online. Make a table with at least fifteen derived words (verbs, maṣdar, participles): word, root, form, meaning in the text. Then write three sentences of yours with three of those words.
